    Industry News: Lea Michele Wants a Scream Queens Reboot, Too

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
    • With multiple projects on the horizon, all eyes are on Lea Michele.
    • Sources indicate that it’s a natural collaboration, as the Bronx-born Michele is the perfect shepherd for a curated NYC experience.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

    With multiple projects on the horizon, all eyes are on Lea Michele. Glee is getting a reboot; fans are begging for Scream Queens to come back, and the actress and singer is about to embark on a tour with Chess co-star Aaron Tveit. She also just starred in Kiehl’s newly introduced “Gift Like a Local” campaign. In partnership with Uber, Michele traveled around to small businesses in New York City and doled out Kiehl’s products. The Glee star even picked most of the stops herself. “Kiehl’s had emailed me and they said, ‘We really want to feature some local businesses in this campaign. Can you send us some of your thoughts?’” she indicates. “It took me about 30 seconds. I had an email with 50 places.”.

    Sources indicate that it’s a natural collaboration, as the Bronx-born Michele is the perfect shepherd for a curated NYC experience. In many ways, she breathes Latest York. She’s starred on Broadway multiple times, most recently in Chess, which just received a Grammy nomination for Best Musical Theater Album. In the later seasons of Glee, her character, Rachel Berry, moved to New York to chase her Broadway dreams (Michele is also rumored to be returning to the show’s reboot). She currently lives in New York with her husband and two children. On the morning of our interview, fresh off a sold-out show with Tveit at the Beacon Theater, she’s having a classic New York morning. “I took my kids to school. I was walking in the sunshine, I had my matcha. I’m getting ready for an event right now,” she says. “It just is a great day.”.

    Below, Michele talks about Glee, her collaboration with Kiehl’s, and whether she’d ever come back for a Scream Queens reboot.

    Recent findings suggest that aaron [Tveit] would love my personal favorite, the Grapefruit Body Cleanser. That’s just my tried-and-true. I used it this morning. If you’re feeling a little tired, it helps you to wake up and feel good. But even if you’re not, if you’re feeling like how I felt this morning, energized and happy, it’s just one of my favorite ways to start the day. Love, love, love their body lotion. It’s one of the only body lotions that I feel like actually works for me and helps to really moisturize my skin. They have all these amazing little kits as well over the holidays. I’ve given my dad Kiehl’s lip balm and eye cream in his stockings every year for the holidays.

    According to recent reports, I’m really excited to be a part of the Kiehl’s family now. I love our commercial that we shot and the fact that we had the opportunity to support some of the local small businesses.

    It has been revealed that I grew up here. I was born in the Bronx. My father owned a deli here in the city. We had ice cream parlors and candy shops. We featured Élan Flowers in my neighborhood. Seasons in Times Square is somewhere that I go all the time and buy flowers for people in Broadway demonstrates. I love Onda, it’s an amazing little facial and wellness store in Tribeca. Obviously, so many little coffee shops. I mean, the list is quite long.

    I just love everything white. I love all-white. My house is all white, but peonies are my favorite flowers. I love hydrangeas. I love white roses. I just love a significant white bouquet of flowers.

    [Aaron Tveit] and I just found out this morning that almost the entire tour sold out. [It] took less than 24 hours. At our show last night, I think we learned so much about what the show is and what the show could be. We had to cut 10 songs from the concert because we just have so much material. I don’t think that we’re going to do the same show every night. I think that each city is going to get their own show. We’re going to do some of what I would say are our greatest hits together, and some of our individual hits that I think that I will always do in concert, but I really just feel like there’s so much that we can do.

    It has been revealed that I want Radio City to be epic. We haven’t really talked about having some friends join us, but that’s also something that we could definitely do if we wanted to and bring out some friends to sing some songs with us. The options are endless.

    It has been revealed that [Aaron is] one of my dearest friends. His wife is one of my closest friends. He’s friends with my husband. Our children are friends. [It’s] amazing that I get to work with someone that I just respect and care about so much.

    It feels awesome. Normally I know when these things are happening, but my publicist texted me in the morning. She was like, “You got a Grammy nomination.” I cried. My reaction was so, even for me, surprising and unexpected. I just broke down. My husband was walking our kids out the door to take them to school, and I was like, “I can’t believe this. We got nominated for a Grammy.” It means so much. I can’t tell you the talent of the cast of Chess. Every single cast member, the most extraordinary talent, our ensemble, the band. To have the cast get this incredible honor, it’s beyond well deserved. I think every single person who saw Chess would agree.

    Sources indicate that we are constantly one-upping each other in the wellness world. He’ll be like, “Have you seen this? Do you have this?” He had some sort of, I don’t know if it was an infrared mat, and I was like, “Okay, I need that. What’s that?” He saw that I had an amazing water filter in my house, and he’s like, “Okay, what’s that? I need that.” He is probably one of the only people who could rival me in my biohacking, wellness, and taking care of myself.

    Most of the time during Chess, if we weren’t talking about Summer House and all of the drama, we were talking about what are all of the wellness things that we’re doing and to try to stay healthy.

    Industry observers note that I’ve been doing Pilates for years. Emma Roberts took me to my first Pilates class when we were living in New Orleans together, shooting Scream Queens. We went to Romney Studios and did a private lesson. I fell in love with it. Since then, I’ve done mat Pilates and hot Pilates and power Pilates. Everything. I felt pretty good going into this, being like, “I know what I need to know.”.

    It wasn’t my first time playing a killer on television, which was also kind of funny. It was so awesome to return to television last night after so many years, and I just had a really great time.

    I met a little girl last night at the meet-and-greet. She was probably 7 years old, and she came to see the concert with her two dads. Her dads were like, “We just are starting to show her some of the musical numbers.” I was like, “Look at you, you’re a little Rachel Berry.” She had her headband on and her cute little penny loafers, and it was just the sweetest thing. What we all created, and what Ryan and Brad and Ian created with Glee, was just so amazing. The things that people say to me about how much it affected their life and brought them so much joy means the world to me.

    I hear stories like that from people all the time, and I know that it really means so much to all of us.

    Sources indicate that the love for Scream Queens has always been there. Emma [Roberts] and I love that show. We talk about it all the time. Ryan knows, too. Ryan and I talk about it always and I beg him all the time. I’m like, “Can we please bring Scream Queens back?” Ryan should do it. It would be awesome.

    It’s so beautiful. I talked a lot about Spring Awakening during my concert last night. We are celebrating 20 years of Spring Awakening opening on Broadway this December. We have a group chat with the original cast. Myself, Lauren Pritchard, and Jonathan Groff are planning a really special private night just for the original cast, a little celebration. I’m so excited that it’s coming to Off-Broadway. My dear, dear, dear sister, Lilli Cooper, is going to be in it. Spring Awakening is such a beautiful and important show, and so anytime that it has the opportunity for people to see it, it should be there. It’s the most beautiful piece of art.

    Oh, yeah. I’ve had the opportunity and the real honor to be a part of some incredible original Broadway productions, both with Ragtime and Spring Awakening. It’s an incredible, incredible show.

    According to recent reports, there are so many. I want to do everything, I really do. I want to do it all. If I am lucky enough to perform on Broadway for the rest of my life, then that would just be the greatest dream. There are so many great shows that have been on Broadway that could be revived and amazing pieces and incredibly talented artists that are writing original pieces as well. So, I’m ready and available for whatever is to come.

    This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If there’s one Apple product line where the recent price hikes hit the hardest, it’s the MacBook.
    • As luck would have it, Black Friday deals on Apple tech have landed on Amazon, with up to 20 percent off MacBooks—including the brand-new M6 MacBook Pros on sale for the first time ever.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If there’s one Apple product line where the recent price hikes hit the hardest, it’s the MacBook. Rising RAM and storage costs have pushed laptop prices up across the board, which makes scoring a fresh MacBook on sale all the more mission critical.

    As luck would have it, Black Friday deals on Apple tech have landed on Amazon, with up to 20 percent off MacBooks—including the brand-new M6 MacBook Pros on sale for the first time ever. Given that these prices have reached record highs lately, these discounts are certainly nothing to sneeze at. In fact, now that the MacBook pricing status quo has been reset, we’d say this is probably as low as MacBook prices will get these days.

    In a recent development, of course, not all MacBooks were created equal. While the standard MacBook Air is great for most, those who are planning on running hardcore software might benefit from a beefed-up MacBook Pro. And if budget is your primary concern, we’re of the opinion that the MacBook Neo is a worthy buy, even if it’s only $50 off right now.

    The best MacBook Air deal you’ll find right now is this $300 discount on the 15-inch model. With this laptop, you’ll get Apple’s M5 chip in a fanless, 3.3-pound frame that handles heavy multitasking and light video editing without breaking a sweat. Base storage doubled to 512 GB this year—a great upgrade for storing more apps, photos, and files—and the 15.3-inch Liquid Retina display is sharp and vivid. You also get a 12 MP Center Stage camera that’s great on video calls, Wi-Fi 7 for fast downloads, and up to 18 hours of battery, enough for a busy workday and then some.

    Industry observers note that if you’d prefer a smaller laptop, 13-inch models are up to 19 percent off. They’ve got everything the 15-inch models have, just in a more portable package. The rule of thumb for choosing between a Pro and an Air? The slimmer Air won’t replace a MacBook Pro for serious creative work or gaming, but for school, business, and general use, it’s the one to get.

    Apple 2026 MacBook Air 13-inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB).

    Apple 2026 MacBook Air 13-Inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB).

    Apple 2026 MacBook Air 15-inch (M5, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB).

    Given that Apple just dropped a fresh slate of M6 MacBook Pros, in addition to the company’s first-ever touchscreen laptop, we were anticipating discounts on the old range of M5 models to clear out inventory. Sure, the best MacBook Pro deal you’ll find right now is $250 off the 14-inch M5 model—but, if you don’t mind paying just $50 more, you can scoop up the shiny new M6 on sale, complete with improved speed and boosted AI capabilities. It’s extremely rare for Apple to discount its latest laptop so soon after release, and even more rare for it to be $200 off.

    Both the M5 and M6 models feature Liquid Retina XDR displays, up to 24 hours of battery, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, an SD card slot, and up to 2 TB of storage.

    Why go Pro over the Air? The GPU is fast, which makes a difference when editing video, working with high-res photos, or gaming, and the XDR screen is significantly brighter. If your daily workload has started becoming too much for the Air to handle, this is where you should look next. If you want the biggest, most powerful model possible, souped-up MacBook Pros with more RAM are up to $500 off.

    Apple 2025 MacBook Pro 14-Inch (M5 Pro, 16 GB RAM, 1 TB).

    Apple 2025 MacBook Pro 14-Inch (M5 Pro, 24 GB RAM, 1 TB).

    Apple 2025 MacBook Pro 16-Inch (M5 Max, 36 GB RAM, 2 TB).

    In a recent development, the MacBook Neo is Apple’s most affordable laptop, even with the recent price hike from $599 to $699. Right now, the Neo is $50 off, sitting smack in the middle between its debut price and post-increase price, at $649—making it far and away the cheapest MacBook.

    It has been revealed that the Neo is an easy recommendation for anyone looking for their first Mac. It runs on Apple’s A18 Pro chip and is surprisingly quick for browsing, sending email, and streaming video. The 13-inch Liquid Retina display looks great for the price, and the battery lasts a solid 16 hours. It also comes in four fun colors, with the yellow-green citrus being a fan favorite.

    There are some trade-offs with going with Apple’s budget model, including storage that starts at 256 GB, just 8 GB of RAM, and no keyboard backlight. You also get only two USB-C ports, so getting a USB-C hub is a must if you plan to connect a lot of accessories. Spending an extra $100 gets you a Neo with 512 GB of storage and a Touch ID sensor for quick unlocking. For students or anyone who mostly sends emails and browses the Web, the Neo is hard to beat.

    • Industry observers note that the allure of soft, understated nails is going nowhere.
    • Industry observers note that for winter, this translates to sheer, milky tones, short, considered nail shapes and microvariations of wearable nail art.
    • Essie Gel Couture Long-Lasting Nail Polish in Liquid Diamonds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the allure of soft, understated nails is going nowhere. Rather, throughout 2026, we’ve seen the minimalist manicure movement gain momentum with each newly introduced season. “It’s the biggest shift I’ve seen in my chair this year,” says celebrity nail technician Iram Shelton. She explains that the theme has been “natural nails, but better,” which is centered around low-maintenance colors and finishes.

    Industry observers note that for winter, this translates to sheer, milky tones, short, considered nail shapes and microvariations of wearable nail art. In preparation for party season, expect to see minuscule flecks of metallic gold and star-themed motifs, too. While milky pink nails will always be in style, this winter, it’s all about unexpected sheers like lavender, bronze, and pearly white. Not only do these colors go with everything, but they also are extremely forgiving—you can paint them on yourself without a problem.

    Zoya Lavender Perfector Nail Polish.

    Londontown Illuminating Nail Concealer in Bare.

    Essie Gel Couture Long-Lasting Nail Polish in Liquid Diamonds.

    Below, find 10 of the most polished, pared-back nail ideas to bookmark for your next appointment.

    Last season, we had Hailey Bieber milk nails, followed by Sienna Miller’s ‘Chantilly cream’. Now? Lavender takes the spotlight, in its dreamiest, near-translucent form. A high-shine top coat makes this tone appear even hazier in the light.

    In a recent development, leaning into minimalism doesn’t necessarily mean forgoing color. Take this rich, berry red for proof; when an all-over pigment isn’t on the cards, a sleek micro French tip is equally flattering.

    It has been revealed that for a simpler take on autumn’s ‘gold fairy dust’ nail trend (as seen on Taylor Swift), draw inspiration from stardust instead. Here, a natural blushed pink base sits beautifully under a gently dazzling, golden shimmer top coat.

    Traditional French tips are given a modern, metallic upgrade without veering into futuristic territory. When reserved for the base of the nail, a gold-toned cuff is eye-catching but in a subtle way.

    Industry observers note that frosted pearlescent finishes are as luminous as they are delicate—not to mention destined for winter weather. When worn with a cozy cashmere knit, you’d be hard-pressed to find a more perfect pairing.

    In a recent development, square and squoval nails are seeing a revival this season. Keep your shapes cropped, softly rounded, and ultra-glossy if committing to minimalism.

    Trade in winter's deep, vibrant mocha, espresso, and cocoa-inspired browns for a sheer bronze pigment. When kept close to the natural nail color, this shade is the best way to embrace elevated color without going overboard.

    According to recent reports, while the notion of nail art might suggest something elaborate colorful, petite star motifs make a case for the opposite. One on each nail balances a feeling of festivity with practicality for everyday wear.

    It has been revealed that granted, a white Christmas might be far on the horizon. But this set sees micro polka dots get a dainty, wintry upgrade, inspired by tiny droplets of snow.

    Sources indicate that if a micro French isn’t your style, an ombré is worth considering. Begin with a nude beige-pink base color, and watch it blend seamlessly into a cozy, seasonal color.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sometimes you luck into a story. Sometimes you’re in the right place at the right time. Sometimes you’re the person in the newsroom who happens to pick up the phone, or the person standing on the corner when the alarm in the bank goes off. Sometimes you’re Abraham Zapruder. And sometimes you’re riding the Metro in D.C. and somebody opens their laptop next to you and reveals something amazing and/or utterly dreadful.

    It is no secret that this administration has had the Smithsonian’s museums in its chicken-greased-fingerprinted sights. It has determined that it was designated by the Almighty to save White People’s History from barbarians of actual historical truth. But how they planned to do it was on the down-low, until an administration apparatchik opened his laptop so that the person sitting next to him could read the planned atrocities, take screenshots of them, and send the screenshots to our friends at ProPublica.

    In which we will be transported back to those glorious days for fourth-grade history class.

    So who was this indiscreet fellow anyway? In Washington, Sparky, the mic is always hot, the camera is always on, and the person next to you on the subway has ProPublica’s phone number.

    In a recent development, the clammy hands of Representative Jim Jordan (R-Van Heusen) should be kept off American history for the same reason that the hands of perverted team physicians are kept off student athletes. Just sayin’.

    #135100. This Forgotten ’90s Comedy Is the Most Demented Thanksgiving Movie Ever

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1754 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    This Forgotten ’90s Comedy Is the Most Demented Thanksgiving Movie Ever

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Let’s start off by acknowledging that the late John Hughes wrote and directed the greatest of all Thanksgiving movies with Planes, Trains and Automobiles.
    • This road-trip saga that Hughes penned and produced in 1991 is by the numbers in most ways but excels in its brazen wrongness, even by the free-range standards of Generation X.
    • According to recent reports, hughes didn’t direct this one, handing off those duties to Peter Faiman, who had worked extensively in Australian TV and only made one other feature film: 1986’s Crocodile Dundee.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Let’s start off by acknowledging that the late John Hughes wrote and directed the greatest of all Thanksgiving movies with Planes, Trains and Automobiles. There are definitely other great ones, but … Dutch is a different kind of creature. This is a Thanksgiving family comedy in which a grown man fights, kidnaps, and abandons a child. Occasionally he holds him at gunpoint. It’s a rotten child but a kid nonetheless. The movie still made me laugh, but it was mostly in disbelief.

    This road-trip saga that Hughes penned and produced in 1991 is by the numbers in most ways but excels in its brazen wrongness, even by the free-range standards of Generation X. I come here to praise this messy movie, not to bury it. It’s a relic from when films could be wilder, shaggier, and more shocking than the rigidly tame family comedies of today. Dutch is many things, but it is not refined to baby-food levels of inoffensive smoothness.

    According to recent reports, hughes didn’t direct this one, handing off those duties to Peter Faiman, who had worked extensively in Australian TV and only made one other feature film: 1986’s Crocodile Dundee. I can’t help but feel this was an experiment gone wrong, or maybe a first draft that needed another pass from Hughes. It’s built out of leftovers from better road-trip movies, and like any Frankenstein’s monster, this one runs straight into a wall and ultimately falls apart.

    But if you want something different for your Thanksgiving watch, go find this one. Fair warning: It’s not streaming anywhere in the United States, so you’ll have to seek it out on a sketchy Russian bootleg site that makes it look like the footage was ripped from a worn-down VHS.

    Dutch stars Ed O’Neill as the title character, a blue-collar guy sent to pick up his girlfriend’s blue-blooded son from a Georgia boarding school and deliver him to Chicago in time for the holiday feast. The not-so-surprising catch is that the kid (played by a 13-year-old Ethan Embry) mercilessly despises Dutch, and honestly the feeling is mutual.

    Doyle is one of the most hateful kids in comedy history. Even the ginger demon of Problem Child was more cartoonishly mischievous than sociopathic. Embry, who was then credited as Ethan Randall, isn’t playing a troublemaking scamp like the kid in O. Henry’s “The Ransom of Red Chief” or Hughes’s own Home Alone. He’s a smug sociopath with a violent mean streak.

    We learn that Dutch is a salt-of-the-earth cousin to O’Neill’s uncouth Al Bundy from Married with Children because he flicks the caviar off his cracker at a fancy party. (“I make it a rule never to eat anything a fish deposits in a riverbed.”) Okay, fair.

    Sources indicate that compare that to how we meet Doyle: Another young boy in his boarding school comes to his room to say he has a call on the dormitory’s community phone line. “Someone from any sort of decent background would knock,” Embry’s character hisses. He then corrects the kid’s vocabulary and threatens to report him to the school administrators for mild cursing. So he’s a snob, a prick, and a rat. But even this is within the bounds of film comedy. You could picture an older version of him as a stuck-up villain in Caddyshack or Animal House.

    Industry observers note that then there’s another, even more disturbing phone scene when Doyle gets the bad news that his rich father won’t be helping him get out of this road trip with Dutch. He hangs up and stalks past an elderly janitor who is sweeping the hallway, silently kicking over the garbage can to scatter trash across the helpless old man’s feet. There’s no joke. He’s just a son of a bitch.

    Doyle would fit in great with the Children of the Corn, except he’d scowl at their shabby farm clothes.

    Recent findings suggest that obviously this kid is going to get some form of comeuppance. When Dutch reveals up at his dorm room to start the trip, Doyle beats him with a golf club and shoots him in the testicles with a BB gun. Something about this is much more violent and visceral than the Looney Tunes–style pratfalls and clobberings of Home Alone.

    Sources indicate that they have a fistfight in the tiny room, and Dutch seizes the weapon. Does he toss it away or break it? No—he uses it himself to hold the kid at gunpoint. We have just crossed beyond the boundaries of comedy, never to return. Dutch then ties the boy up, lashes him to a hockey stick for easier carrying, and stuffs underwear in his mouth to muffle his cries.

    You know a movie is going off the rails when watching it makes you feel like you should be testifying against the characters as a witness for the prosecution.

    Sources indicate that so begins the drive, with Dutch and Doyle doing their best to annoy each other verbally. Then comes a bizarre scene in which Dutch stops for fireworks for some reason and sets them off in a snowy field while the kid watches from the car. I suppose he’s trying to inspire a little playfulness in the boy, but it just seems like Dutch has lost it and is indulging a pyromaniac streak.

    Industry observers note that it goes wrong and he sets his coat on fire, which makes it harder to understand why he loses his temper when the boy flicks the butt of his lit cigar at him. The man just went mano a mano with a whizzing fireworks spinner, but this is what lights his fuse?

    Dutch does the reasonable thing. He abandons the boy in the snowy night and tells him to walk the rest of the way to the motel. “About 50 miles down the road!” Fifty miles? Okay, Dutch, I believe we’ve added another felony to the charges.

    This isn’t one of those moments where the grown-up pulls over just beyond the tree line and waits for him. Dutch actually goes to the hotel, although he occasionally puts down his paperback and checks the window to see if the boy has made it there alive. When Doyle finally does show up, shivering and wet, Dutch says, “Here’s something you should know about me. I don’t fool around. You piss me off, I react.”.

    Uncle Buck certainly had its off-color and irresponsible moments, but even that havoc-prone babysitter might have called Child Protective Services over this situation.

    Industry observers note that doyle responds by stealing Dutch’s car keys while he sleeps and parking the sedan sideways in the snowy road, where it is slammed into by an 18-wheeler. This is a comedy, so the hapless truck driver is not killed on impact.

    Sources indicate that faiman shoots all of this with too much gritty realism. Maybe it would work if it was all a little zanier and over the top (think of Vacation), but Dutch just plays less like a series of set pieces and more like an array of crime scenes. They don’t call anyone for help because Dutch doesn’t want to admit to his girlfriend how badly things are going, so they hitchhike the rest of the way and stay in a homeless shelter, where the rotten kid learns that a lot of people have it much worse than he does.

    It has been revealed that at one point, they are picked up by a pair of pretty young women who are driving home from a job at the Superdome in New Orleans. “We’re call girls,” one of them explains. Hoo boy. Here we go.

    But thankfully—mercifully—Dutch goes no further than showing the kid sleeping in the backseat with his head resting on the chest of one of the women. Not great, but it could be worse. (Worse is when Dutch tries to bond with the child over a deck of naked playing cards.).

    Industry observers note that even Dutch seems to recognize that “prostitute road trip” probably isn’t the ideal situation for a young boy. But he explains it in the most vulgar way possible: “You and I are riding in the backseat from now on, because what that missile twister can teach you, you don’t need to learn until you’re in prison.” Then the ladies drive off without them, taking Dutch’s wallet and leaving the pair stranded again.

    Sources indicate that they spend the next leg of their trip riding in the open concrete pipes in the back of a long-haul truck, but they fall asleep and wake up in a trailer depot where they are roughed up by two security guards. Doyle responds by drawing his BB gun on them and making them believe he is going to blow their heads off.

    Recent findings suggest that this same joke was deployed by Chevy Chase in the Hughes-scripted National Lampoon’s Vacation (“Are you kidding, this is a Magnum P.I.”) but here, again, it just plays as psychotic violence rather than absurd humor. “The kid is crazy,” Dutch tells the men as they beg for their lives.

    In a recent development, by the time the duo finally get home for the Thanksgiving meal, the hostility between Dutch and the kid has softened into a grudging respect. I know: Surprise! Back at the mother’s house, Dutch physically assaults the boy’s callous father, leaving a mark with his pinkie ring on the jerk’s forehead. Instead of an assault charge, it all ends happily ever after with a callback to an earlier gag: Dutch pulls the BB pistol from his pocket and claims it’s time to get the revenge he promised he would one day seek. As the boy’s smile fades, Dutch aims the gun at him—and us (!!!)—as the film cuts to the credits.

    According to recent reports, oh, Dutch … you dangerously inappropriate maniac. Don’t ever change. And, well, he doesn’t, although the kid goes through the expected metamorphosis to become a more sensitive and understanding human.

    Industry observers note that they don’t make ’em like this anymore, as the saying goes, and I actually think that’s a pity. Dutch isn’t all that funny, but neither is toothless humor that’s overly safe. I’d gladly tolerate a few misfires like this if it meant more truly unhinged comedies like we had in the ’80s, ’90s, and early 2000s. Dutch stands as a throwback to when small-scale comedies weren’t afraid to take big swings—even if they occasionally landed against someone’s skull or testicles.

    #135094. Blade Runner 2099 Is a Beautiful Slog Through a Grim Future

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (655 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    Blade Runner 2099 Is a Beautiful Slog Through a Grim Future

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (655 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that crowded streets.
    • Streaming now on Prime Video (and just in time for a long holiday weekend) is Blade Runner 2099.
    • In a recent development, hunter Schafer flexes some of her budding leading-lady chops as Cora, a real human posing as a Replicant to smuggle herself and her brother out of Los Angeles.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that crowded streets. Long, cool coats. Flying cars darting through smog and neon skyscrapers. An abundance of Japanese aesthetics that imply America’s lost superpower status. Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 masterwork Blade Runner (itself adapted from Philip K. Dick’s Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?) laid the foundation for almost all of cyberpunk science fiction, so much so that everything else feels undeservedly derivative. Even a new Blade Runner. The new series Blade Runner 2099 looks the part, but it lacks the soul of its predecessors, leaving its perspectives on what it means to be more human than human hollow, like a Replicant without memories of its own.

    Streaming now on Prime Video (and just in time for a long holiday weekend) is Blade Runner 2099. A stand-alone continuation of both Ridley Scott’s towering original and Denis Villeneuve’s remarkable legacy sequel, the series takes place in 2099 (decades after Villeneuve’s Blade Runner 2049). An unseen revolution has elevated Replicants to the ruling class of Los Angeles, rendering flesh-and-bone meat-bag humans as the new discriminated minority.

    In a recent development, hunter Schafer flexes some of her budding leading-lady chops as Cora, a real human posing as a Replicant to smuggle herself and her brother out of Los Angeles. Her ruse leads her to Olwen (Oscar-winner Michelle Yeoh), a Replicant Blade Runner spending the final days of her artificial life span seeking out someone from her past. A humorless buddy-cop mystery, Blade Runner 2099 is mired in a plot-centric narrative that cares less about the why of all things—an underrated and beautiful feature of its predecessors—than the what and how.

    Sources indicate that in other words, it’s the first time a piece of Blade Runner media actually zeroes in on the plot, instead of anything else more interesting. Try not to think of this as an eight-hour Blade Runner series but rather an eight-hour series stretching at the seams to feel worthy of its branded title.

    Is it because streaming TV in 2026 has become so plastic and hollow that even Blade Runner 2099 feels like an unengaging slog? Or were the direction of both Scott and Villeneuve so immaculate that we were distracted from how turgid they might have been all this time? Regardless, 2099’s lack of auteurship is its most deafening shortcoming. The series has been steered to the screen by executive producer Silka Luisa, whose warmer color palettes—based on her choice of more sunshine, which glistens off surfaces—lend 2099 some identity. Some.

    Industry observers note that but beyond even that minor distinction, Blade Runner 2099 is still just a plot-y crime drama that checks off boxes and goes through the motions of its genre, with nary a real thing to say. About us, about our fragile humanity, about the demise of all we’ve built through artificial intelligence. Blade Runner 2099 is a dystopian sci-fi in all the ways you expect it, but it’s hardly a good one. Sure, the original movies were oppressive, dreary, and morbid too. But they possessed a knowing glare into our fears about the future and our imminent collapse as a civilized species. The upcoming series lacks this same insight, or indeed any of its own, all in the name of goosing up engagement numbers for the closest thing to a real-life Tyrell Corp. (Do shareholders dream of electric quarterly reports?).

    Despite surface-level similarities to the movies, plus a moody noir-like motif with a sexy saxophone that, admittedly, completely and unapologetically rips, the plodding Blade Runner 2099 is a needless walkabout through a world that never begged for one. Needless is a good word, actually. The show’s strong visual execution is negated by its inability to rise to the occasion as a worthwhile or enlightening probe of the human experience, or even just as an entertaining cop show. It may be smart, but what good is intelligence if there isn’t an ounce of grace?

    You Don’t Need Designer Sneakers. You Need These $95 German Army Trainers.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (665 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor.
    • These picks are the best way to spend your hard-earned cash.
    • In my life, I lean toward luxury and secondhand clothing wherever possible, desperately trying to get away from all the cheap garbage being sold to me on Instagram ads and the Amazon homepage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

    Welcome to the Esquire Endorsement. Heavily researched. Thoroughly vetted. These picks are the best way to spend your hard-earned cash.

    In my life, I lean toward luxury and secondhand clothing wherever possible, desperately trying to get away from all the cheap garbage being sold to me on Instagram ads and the Amazon homepage. I’ve spent years of my life hunting sales and eBay listings for clothes and boots. I’m like an edge-habitat pine growing in the direction of the radiant sun that is well-made clothing, trying to forget the fast fashion slop that lies in the forest behind me.

    Recent findings suggest that but I throw that out the window when it comes to sneakers. Designer sneakers are, for me, one of the dumbest things I could ever buy. Even when they are made with real leather, you are paying for a plastic sole that has a lifespan of a few years. I don’t think you should pay more than the $200 price of a pair of Newly introduced Balance when it comes to sneakers.

    Under that price point, I’ve never been able to find a good pair German Army Trainers, which I have always wanted. That changed when I found these. Quince (yeah yeah, I was just complaining about fashion slop, but life is full of contradictions) makes a perfect pair of GATs—and it makes them for $95. I honestly think every man in the world should buy a pair of these.

    Recent findings suggest that this is my real qualm with designer sneakers, and it totally undercuts anything you could tell me about the second-hand sneaker hype market. What you should pay for, when you pay expensive prices for clothing, is craftsmanship. When you buy a Gucci 1953 loafer or Loro Piana cashmere you probably arrived there because of the brand, but you are paying for the craftsmanship. I see no such correlation in designer sneakers, even the ones those brands make.

    Recent findings suggest that but a $95 pair of kicks? That’s honest. Even though I’m not bullish on Quince’s fast fashion take on quiet luxury (nor am I bullish on its caviar program), and the fact that Quince chose to closely replicate the Margiela GAT instead of the original German army models, I will let it slide. At $95, there are no claims being made about leather quality, or the footbed, or whatever is going on in the sole you can’t see. They look good and are easy to replace; it’s about as honest of a deal as you can find shopping these days.

    The thing about the original BW Sport GATs—which you can get for about this price still, though used workout sneakers aren’t my cup of tea—is that they’re just about bulletproof. Those original mid-century designs made were first issued in the 1970s and stopped being issued around the end of the Cold War, a real feat of durability.

    These shoes mimic that Army-issued durability. I’ve worn these sneakers for going on a year now. In that time, I’ve seen many pairs of more expensive kicks start to fall apart, get scuffed beyond recognition, and stink like hell. These have not. The pair I’ve worn all year is the pair pictured in this story. Nothing I say in this endorsement could be more convincing than that.

    Recent findings suggest that and really that’s the argument here. When I wrote about the Chuck Taylors I normally wear, it was a use-it-and-lose-it argument—they cost $45, who cares if the soles get holes within 12 months. But here, I fear I’m going to sound like a marketing mouthpiece for Quince. These shoes are $95, but they’ll last just as long as a pair that cost you $950. That’s all you can ask for these days.

Now, it's lower quality and costs more money. Reproductions of what used to be American working clothes now easily cost $300 or more. C'est la vie.

The 517, Levi's take on a Western cut, is going for a discount. And the 501—which I don't love in its modern iteration, but cannot deny the popularity of—is hovering just below $50, depending on the size and wash. Depending on the jeans you buy, you’re getting a discount of between 19 and 43 percent for the best cheap denim out there. If you're looking for a newly introduced jacket, which Levi's still makes decent versions of, Amazon has deals on two sherpa trucker jackets. Go with the classic denim for $63 or opt for the corduroy for $85.

    In a recent development, all right, that's enough explaining. Pick what speaks to you. Buy it. Then, go forth a new man with refreshed style.

    #135080. Tech Report: 42 Designer-Approved Playroom Ideas That Prove Kids’ Spaces Can Still Look Stylish

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1120 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: 42 Designer-Approved Playroom Ideas That Prove Kids’ Spaces Can Still Look Stylish

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1120 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As much as you love your children, you may not love living among their toys and furniture.
    • Whether you lean toward the “beige mom” style or prefer a more maximalist interior, these playroom ideas offer something special for you and your children.
    • Kids are always changing their minds about what they want, so keep things a bit more fluid in their playroom with a modular sofa that they can constantly rearrange.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As much as you love your children, you may not love living among their toys and furniture. People spend a lot of time, effort, and money making their homes look beautiful, but not every design choice is kid-friendly—or built to withstand little ones. If you have room for a dedicated play space, outside of your children’s bedrooms, it could provide the perfect solution to let them be as messy and imaginative as possible. And a playroom can still be aesthetically pleasing, too. Take a look at these designer spaces for inspiration.

    Whether you lean toward the “beige mom” style or prefer a more maximalist interior, these playroom ideas offer something special for you and your children.

    Additional copy by Hadley Mendelsohn.

    Kids are always changing their minds about what they want, so keep things a bit more fluid in their playroom with a modular sofa that they can constantly rearrange. In this kids’ space, designer Kate Haynes of Noble Studio chose to put this sofa underneath the climbing wall for a soft place to land.

    It has been revealed that in this calming playroom, Mandy Cheng added wraparound cabinetry to store all the toys and crafts her clients’ children have accumulated over the years. It not only gives the room a clear purpose, but the closed cabinet doors make the space feel so much cleaner.

    An unused corner in designer Ali Budd’s home became the ultimate play area for her kids. “It has a play structure, cushions, curtains, and Gucci wallpaper,” Budd says. “Somehow this tiny kids’ space ended up being one of the chicest spaces in the house.”.

    Just because the playroom is for the kids, doesn’t mean their walls should be bare. In this room designed by Katie Davis, she went with cute Goldfish cracker-themed 3D artwork, alluding to the children’s favorite snack.

    Industry observers note that the furniture in this playroom, designed by Hilary Colia and Jennifer Kostohryz of Fort Design Studio, actually came from the old family room. It gives the space a more elevated and timeless feel, even when it’s purposely designed for the kids, and it gives the parents a comfortable place to sit.

    Designer Emory McKim knew her kids would want to be anywhere she and her husband were, so she designed their playroom to be connected to the den via a cased opening. “It has worked seamlessly for us,” McKim claims. “We can be in the den enjoying a show, while also watching the kids.”.

    Sources indicate that in this older playroom, designer Alden Fletcher picked out a dark green wallpaper to top the knotty pine wainscoting, then went with other deep earthy tones to make up the space. It’s cozy and inviting, and the ski-themed pattern on the wallcovering keeps it feeling youthful, but not immature.

    According to recent reports, if your kids have (reasonable!) design requests for their playroom, making them come true will give them the space of their dreams. In this animal-accented playroom, designer Ariel Okin says that the kids “really wanted a swinging chair,” so she added one.

    According to recent reports, add playfulness to the room by choosing a fun, patterned floor. The team at Becca Interiors chose this white, black, and burnt orange carpet for the playroom in this Connecticut home, giving the space a bit more life and vibrancy.

    According to recent reports, A Dutch door is a playroom idea that bridges the gap between whimsical and practical. It encloses the space while letting you promptly peek in if needed. The team at Curated Nest chose to do so in this upstate Upcoming York home, and it matches the rest of the aesthetic perfectly.

    In the same home as above, Curated Nest installed this custom climbing wall in the basement. “The kids are very active and wanted a space for friends to enjoy, so we created this custom climbing wall with a hand-painted mural,” Lina Galvão from Curated Nest explains.

    In a recent development, yes, the playroom in your home should appeal to the little ones, but that doesn't mean you have to sacrifice your entire aesthetic. Designer Annie Kern did not shy away from the rich tones and textures that make up the rest of the house in this playroom idea.

    Recent findings suggest that combine a playroom and bunk room for the ultimate sleepover space. Designer Becca Casey added built-in shelves and a window seat to this moody space. Plus, there are three separate beds so the kids can have plenty of overnight playdates.

    A hand-painted mural is the stuff of playroom dreams—it will encourage imaginative play and give your children the fondest memories of growing up in such a beautiful space. In this home, designer Tina Ramchandani used a ceiling mural to add color without feeling chaotic.

    As your kids get older and their interests change, their personal space should evolve too. What was once a playroom covered in stuffed animals may become a pint-sized workspace for arts and crafts. Designer Marika Meyer claims that this colorful, inspiring craft room might just be her favorite in the entire project.

    Decorate the kids-only space with art that they've done themselves. Do what designer Ashley Gilbreath did in this playroom idea and showcase their artwork in custom frames—it'll make your children feel so special to see their work on display.

    As designer Emily Henderson points out, kids outgrow things swiftly—what they love today, they could be bored of tomorrow. “Keep large pieces neutral,” she notes. “It's easier and more affordable to layer on pops of color and your kids' favorite characters or animals than it is to implement those motifs into the furniture and rugs.”.

    Implement traditional patterns and elegant materials when figuring out your playroom ideas—it doesn't have to be all neon and bright colors. Designer Becca Casey added a beautiful toile print wallpaper and rattan accents to this room that will only get better with time.

    Related Story: Toile de Jouy: The Famous French Pattern’s History and Enduring Appeal.

    If your home has a small, awkwardly sized space, put the playroom in there. This reading nook in a boy's room by Benni Amadi was designed to feel like an indoor tree fort. Utilizing as much square footage in the house as possible and having fun with it was key.

    Related Story: 12 Closet Remodeling Projects That Will Transform Your Space.

    Teach your kids early on about the importance of separating work and home life by designing a little study area for them in their playroom. As they grow older and start working on homework after school, their desk space can mature with them, like in this space by Marika Meyer.

    A Landmark All-Lalanne Sale Is Heading to Sotheby’s

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elledecor

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The market for Claude and François-Xavier Lalanne’s irreverent creations has been on a high lately.
    • Industry observers note that now, ELLE Decor can exclusively share that Sotheby’s will host the first-ever auction dedicated to Les Lalanne, featuring pieces sourced from various collections.
    • It has been revealed that “Les Lalanne have become a global phenomenon, changing the way generations of collectors think about design,” claims Jodi Pollack, chairman of 20th century design and major collections for the Americas.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The market for Claude and François-Xavier Lalanne’s irreverent creations has been on a high lately. In April, a single wooly sheep sculpture by François-Xavier fetched $2.3 million. Over the summer, a quartet of his frog fountains smashed their $3.5 million estimate to achieve nearly $6.3 million. And the record for most expensive collectible design work belongs to a set of flower-adorned bronze mirrors crafted by Claude: They netted $33.5 million earlier this year, eclipsing François-Xavier’s $31.4 million hippo bar.

    Industry observers note that now, ELLE Decor can exclusively share that Sotheby’s will host the first-ever auction dedicated to Les Lalanne, featuring pieces sourced from various collections. On December 8, more than 30 works by the late French artist duo will hit the block in “Les Lalanne: Beyond Imagination.” It is expected to fetch in the region of $25 million.

    It has been revealed that “Les Lalanne have become a global phenomenon, changing the way generations of collectors think about design,” claims Jodi Pollack, chairman of 20th century design and major collections for the Americas. “A sheep can be a seat, a crocodile can be a console, and both can hold their own alongside the most important works in a collection.”.

    The collection spans everything from a gold-patinated bronze gorilla (estimated at $8–12 million) to a white marble owl (estimated at $4–6 million), and a flock of five sheep, including two lambs ($300,000–500,000 each). Highlights also include lesser-known motifs, such as a playful pair of bronze monkeys with deep-green patination that makes them almost look like jade ($800,000–1.2 million each), and two matching crocodile consoles ($700,000–1 million) that complement the famous chairs Claude created after obtaining a deceased crocodile from the Paris Zoo.

    In a recent development, those hoping to get an in-person glimpse at the creatures can see the menagerie starting December 2 at the Breuer building, Sotheby’s new Manhattan headquarters. To accompany the show, the auction house enlisted Milan-based artist Gaia Alari to devise custom illustrations for the catalogue, which reads like a fairy tale.

    “The story begins in the catalogue and comes to life at the Breuer, where visitors will step into an enchanted winter garden and meet the cast,” states Pollack. “It’s our way of celebrating these works and the spirit in which they were conceived. We want visitors to look at familiar things as Claude and François-Xavier did and to see the extraordinary in the ordinary.”.

    “Les Lalanne: Beyond Imagination” will be on view at Sotheby’s Upcoming York from December 2 to 7. The live auction will take place on December 8, 2026, at Sotheby’s New York at 11 a.m..

    In a recent development, geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

    • Fashion can’t get enough of freaky hats lately.
    • Simone Rocha’s sequin-embellished bonnets with chin straps might turn you into a living doll.

    Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

    Fashion can’t get enough of freaky hats lately. Following the main character hat trend from a few seasons past, this time headwear has gone totally theatrical and over-the-top. Between Chanel’s fin-embellished Nemo-esque swim caps and Junya Watanabe’s super camp, oversize ’70s baker-boy-style caps, headpieces are seemingly obsessed with transforming their wearers into outlandish personas. And at a time when clothing is centered on escapism and storytelling, an eccentric chapeau might just be the most perfect finishing touch.

    Simone Rocha’s sequin-embellished bonnets with chin straps might turn you into a living doll. Celebs, too, have already gotten the memo: Elle Fanning recently wore a Stephen Jones-designed makeup compact headpiece to match her Givenchy dress inspired by an archival piece he created over three decades ago, while doing press for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. Elsewhere, Cardi B revealed up in a white embellished gown from Tamara Ralph’s spring 2026 couture collection, styled with a huge, showgirl-style feather hat. Ciara walked the Junya Watanabe spring/summer 2027 runway while wearing a bedazzled helmet dripping with chains.

    Sources indicate that at Vaquera’s spring/summer 2027 show titled “I’m a put-on-a-show kind of girl,” the neon high-octane gowns were counterbalanced with huge, satirical boater hats, followed by a weird and whimsical chef hat and maid headpiece paired with shrunken, mini bloomer uniform onesies. Adding more humor to the collection, the designers ended the show by performing a live karaoke version of Sonny & Cher’s “I Got You Babe.” The brand is the king of the theatrical character hat. For fall/winter 2026, it showcased pillbox-style hats that eclipsed the face with cutouts for the eyes, fencing-mask-inspired headwear, and an elongated train conductor hat that resembles a cross between The Rockettes Toy Soldier costumes and English bearskin caps.

    Transforming is exactly the point: “Vaquera has always celebrated fashion’s transformative power,” read Vaquera’s show notes. “The collection confronts the tension between perfection and chaos. Can you be unhinged and complete at once? Its cast of characters—distorted drab mods, twisted ladies who lunch, abstracted leather daddies—all seem to suggest that the most covetable clothes for your future are those that mirror our fractured present.”.

    While years of the past were defined by singular aesthetics, 2026 lacks one solo homogeneous style. Formality, too, has been traded for casual looks. Hats used to be ubiquitous; now they’re sort of a rare dying breed, save for a baseball cap.

    In a recent development, perhaps that’s one of the reasons why these character-driven hats are so prevalent now. Many of them are tied to uniforms, occupations, or the everyday made extreme. It’s beautiful absurdism, verging on delightfully unhinged. Consider an over-the-top hat pure whimsy.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Few hair colors are as iconic and instantly nostalgic as Geri Halliwell's natural red. The hue, synonymous with her nickname “Ginger Spice,” has, of course, evolved over the years, from copper highlights woven through fiery red lengths to a full head of golden blond and lighter strawberry-blond tones.

    Recent findings suggest that for winter, Halliwell has swapped her signature brighter tones for a richer shade. Enter dark honey hair. "What I absolutely love about Geri’s dark honey hair is the richness and depth of the color. A beautiful chestnut base with ribbons of warm honey, caramel, and subtle amber runs through the lengths and ends. It’s a wonderful evolution of her signature warmth, but with a softer, more understated finish," notes celebrity hairstylist and Remi Cachet expert Adam Reed.

    At the premiere of Only Murders in London, Halliwell wore her fresh hair color in a soft side part with dressed-out waves, a combination Reed states helps different tones catch the light.

    Recent findings suggest that the rich, luminous color adds subtle dimension that doesn't focus on dramatic placement, but on healthy-looking hair. "To recreate the look, I’d ask your colorist to maintain that beautiful brunette depth through the roots, introducing delicately placed honey and caramel lights through the mid-lengths and ends. A personalized gloss can bring those tones together and create that beautifully reflective finish," he adds.

    Alternatively, Reed recommends his “just a little filler” approach, using extensions as color tools placed strategically. This approach uses additional hair to enhance color, density, and movement, rather than focusing solely on length. "By carefully selecting complementary shades of chestnut, honey, and caramel, we can introduce tonal variation without necessarily having to chemically lighten the natural hair," he notes.

    Whether you're looking for a complete hair refresh this winter or simply want a subtle way to enhance your natural color without fully committing to a new look, Halliwell's dark honey hair is the perfect inspiration.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (910 w)

    Latest Update: Inside Anmer Hall, Kate Middleton and Prince William’s Country Retreat

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday.
    • In a recent development, local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times.
    • Industry observers note that anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday. Two masked men reportedly broke into Anmer Hall, their Georgian estate in Norfolk. Located on the grounds of the Sandringham Estate, the landmark house is where the Prince and Princess of Wales like to spend holidays and weekends with their three children, and it was also where Catherine recuperated from surgery and cancer treatments in 2024.

    In a recent development, local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times. The estate itself was unoccupied at the time of the break-in, according to police, and the suspects remain in custody.

    Industry observers note that anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage. It’s a royal residence filled with equal parts gravitas and style. Take a closer look inside below.

    In a recent development, anmer Hall is in the quaint village of Anmer in Norfolk, a coastal county in northeastern England about a three-hour drive from London. The ten-bedroom Georgian pile, built in 1802, is part of Sandringham Estate, a sprawling 20,000-acre property dotted with churches, parishes, and country houses, that has been connected to the royals since 1862. The estate’s grand residence, Sandringham House, is the country bolthole of King Charles III and Queen Camilla, where royal Christmases are famously hosted. Anmer Hall is just a five-minute drive away.

    While you can book tours of Sandringham House and even rent properties on the greater estate, Anmer Hall is a private family residence. The village of Anmer includes a church and quaint cottages, many of which were built in the early 20th century for Edward VII, according to an architectural guide to Norfolk by Nikolaus Pevsner and Bill Wilson. The U.K.’s Office for National Statistics states that Anmer parish had a population of about 250 in 2017.

    Sources indicate that anmer Hall was the seat of the Coldham family until Prince Albert Edward (aka the future Edward VII) purchased it in 1896 to be a part of the Sandringham Estate, Pevsner and Wilson note. The two-story house’s “charming” brick facade, made from red and brown brick, features 13 bays and dormer windows in the attic. The house underwent renovations in the years following Edward VII’s purchase.

    Over the next century, the house was leased to numerous members of the British aristocracy, including the Duke and Duchess of Kent from 1972 to 1990, and Hugh van Cutsem, one of King Charles III’s best friends. Following the expiration of van Cutsem’s lease, the property was rented to timber tech giant owner James Everett.

    It has been revealed that in 2013, two years after William and Kate’s marriage, it was rumored that the royal couple would be moving in. The pair had been renting a farmhouse in Anglesey, off the northwest coast of Wales, while Prince William worked as a helicopter pilot and while they were expecting their first child, Prince George. “[Anmer Hall] would seem to be an ideal choice in that it’s close to Grandma—but not too close,” former royal correspondent Michael Cole told the BBC. Later that year, it was confirmed that William and Kate would be moving into their new “baby bunker” with Prince George. But they wouldn’t physically move in until two years later, when Kate was expecting their second child, Princess Charlotte, to allow time for a $2 million refurbishment, which included a new roof, additional trees for privacy, and interior improvements.

    In 2017, Meghan Markle and Prince Harry stayed with William and Kate at Anmer Hall, “because the sovereign still won’t permit unwed couples to sleep together under her roof Sandringham,” according to the book Notorious Royal Marriages by Leslie Carroll.

    Today, the Prince and Princess of Wales spend most of their time at their upcoming primary royal residence Forest Lodge on the grounds of Windsor Castle—but they use Anmer as a country escape. The family also spent the Covid lockdown at Anmer Hall.

    As part of the property’s improvements, the Prince and Princess of Wales tapped architect Charles Morris for the renovation and designer Ben Pentreath—the designer who overhauled Kate and William’s apartment at Kensington Palace, per House & Garden—for the interiors.

    It has been revealed that pentreath’s firm describes its approach as one “that draws inspiration in equal measure from the great English practitioners of the 18th and 19th centuries, and from the 1960s and ’70s…but always infused with a fresh, modern sensibility”—and the same style can be seen in snippets of Anmer Hall that eagle-eyed viewers have spotted in the Prince and Princess of Wales’s social media feeds. The home—with its high ceilings and decorative moldings—is painted in soothing, neutral colors (though the dining room is reportedly a deep green hue) and accessorized with houseplants, antiques, and gilt-framed art.

    Additional amenities on the property include a pool and a tennis court; Anmer Hall also hosts its own honeybee colony. And one last bonus: The home is even said to be haunted by its own ghost.

    Recent findings suggest that geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By MoonSwatch standards, it’s been a quiet year.
    • An estimated 4.5 million have been sold since the collaboration began in March 2022 (and that figure only takes us to the end of 2024).
    • The latest MoonSwatch—only the third fresh model this year, compared with 11 in 2023—is the Mission to Earthphase – Silver Snowflake.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By MoonSwatch standards, it’s been a quiet year. Swatch has been otherwise occupied with the Audemars Piguet Royal Pop, the May release for which people lined up for six days in Newly introduced York, police deployed tear gas in France, and which, according to Swatch Group, has generated more than 25 billion views on social media.

    Not that interest in the MoonSwatch has gone away.

    An estimated 4.5 million have been sold since the collaboration began in March 2022 (and that figure only takes us to the end of 2024). In July this year, some 1.2 million people applied to buy one of the 1,969 examples of its $570 Mission to the Moon 1969, a watch that incorporated 11 grams of 18-carat gold recycled from vintage Omega components.

    The latest MoonSwatch—only the third fresh model this year, compared with 11 in 2023—is the Mission to Earthphase – Silver Snowflake.

    An all-black counterpart to last winter’s all-white Cold Moon edition, it takes as its starting point the idea that no two snowflakes are alike.

    Swatch has developed a digital process capable of generating millions of different snowflake patterns, one of which is laser-engraved onto the moonphase indicator of each watch. So, unusually for a mass-produced quartz watch, every example is unique.

    It also features the complication Swatch introduced in November 2024 and which remains exclusive to the MoonSwatch: an earthphase indicator. Where a conventional moonphase highlights the phases of the Moon as viewed from Earth, this does the reverse. The two displays run in opposite directions over the same 29.5-day cycle.

    (How useful this is to those of us who live on Earth is debatable, but it’s one of the more original ideas in watchmaking in recent years.).

    There are some nice details elsewhere on the 42mm Bioceramic watch, including Snoopy and Woodstock in the snow, a pair of miniature skis at 11 o’clock, and a tiny patch of white on the Earth representing a snow-covered Switzerland, which glows green under UV light.

    As with last year’s winter edition, there’s a stipulation.

    In a recent development, the watch goes on sale at selected Swatch stores worldwide on Black Friday, November 27. After that, until March 20, 2027, the last day of winter, you’ll only be able to buy one when it’s snowing in Switzerland.

    Swatch will be providing weather updates on its website.

    Like any specialized skill set, winter layering is one that must be continually practiced and perfected, lest your talents wane. It’s not as easy as throwing on a pair of cashmere leggings and a coordinating hoodie—that’s only the beginning. From there, it takes a careful curation of hero pieces (like puffer jackets and parkas), as well as a cast of supporting details (hats, gloves, and high-performance footwear), to layer effectively and aesthetically in the harshest conditions.

    That remarked, even the most adept artist is nothing without an arsenal of trusted creative tools. And in these bitter temps, you’ll want to reach for the best, which essentially means any piece of gear with The North Face’s iconic rectangular logo attached to it. The storied brand has dominated the outdoor space for decades, having perfected the art of elevated style at elevated altitudes.

    Recent findings suggest that as we head into the chilliest season of the year, look to The North Face’s vast selection of dependable staples for all your layering needs. Designed both for performance and appearances, these pieces are in it for the long run.

    Whether painting or dressing, it’s essential to start any creative endeavor with a blank canvas made of quality materials. A good base should be versatile and simple to pair with a host of helpful staples. Long-sleeve tees, cashmere turtlenecks, and crewneck sweatshirts, for example, are all good jumping-off points.

    Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for a high-performance piece with enough style power to stand on its own, we recommend the Women’s Chabot 2.0 Mock-Neck. This cozy layering top offers the same reliable comfort of a traditional insulated thermal with a few modern updates. Though understated by design, its delightfully oversized fit and a funky waffle knit texture make the basic feel intentional and interesting.

    For a closer-fitting base, the Women’s Golden Ridge Ribbed Long-Sleeve Tee layers easily under other pieces. Its slim fit and ribbed texture give this practical layer a polished look, while thumbholes at the cuffs add a functional detail. Bonus points for the tee’s anti-odor technology that helps keep the fabric feeling fresh.

    Women’s Golden Ridge Ribbed Long-Sleeve Tee.

    Sources indicate that after you’ve selected the first layer, the next stop should be your coat closet. This is where you’ll select the hero of your look. While each piece of the layering puzzle is uniquely crucial, the power jacket is a non-negotiable. The right iteration should supply a thick layer of warmth, while also doing its part to make the outfit, as a whole, feel cohesive.

    Those who crave a more subdued winter aesthetic will love the classic appeal of the Women’s Arctic Bomber. The waterproof winter jacket boasts all the utility of a parka, with the sleek design details most commonly found in trend-focused outerwear. In four comforting colorways, this winter coat is an insulation powerhouse in a chic, wearable package.

    Look to the Women’s Hydrenalite Down Jacket for a more classic puffer. This workhorse is a versatile down layer that can be slipped on at any time to keep you warm for any duration that you spend outdoors, whether you are on the mountain or running around town.

    For the more artistically inclined, try the Women’s Yumiori Off Peak Full Zip Jacket. This fleece outer layer offers unfailing warmth and a distinctly sporty flavor. Its two-tone color palette, meanwhile, adds a fun, whimsical feel to the utilitarian, zip-up-style silhouette.

    Women’s Hydrenalite Down Jacket.

    Women’s Yumiori Off Peak Full Zip Jacket.

    It has been revealed that during the summer months, it’s all about the mani-pedi. But once that icy weather blows in, self-care starts to look a bit different. The North Face’s Etip Gloves are basically a hand treatment on the go. Crafted from soft, stretchy fleece made with 93 percent recycled polyester, these tech-friendly gloves will keep your hands comfortable on cold-weather outings. They’ll also keep you connected: Touchscreen compatibility lets you check your phone without taking them off, while silicone grip dots on the palms help you hold onto your device as well as smaller essentials like keys and credit cards.

    Recent findings suggest that for footwear, the Women’s THERMOBALL Traction Mule V will promptly become the standout of your seasonal lineup. These cloud-like slip-ons pair warm insulation with a quilted upper that gives them a casual, streetwear-cool vibe. The rubber outsole adds traction for quick trips outdoors.

    Women’s THERMOBALL Traction Mule V.

    Recent findings suggest that the minimalist philosophy requires you to take off one item before leaving the house. But during the cold weather season, it’s in your best interest to do the opposite. As you walk out the door, make sure you grab a beanie since most of your body heat can escape from your head.

    Beanies are simultaneously the most underappreciated outfit addition and the most indispensable. The North Face’s Wool Blend Beanie, for instance, pairs the warmth of its 65 percent merino wool knit with a refined, metropolitan style. Its classic cuffed design and textured knit add visual interest, while its deep fit offers roomier coverage. If you prefer the rectangular logo with the same cuffed look, you can never go wrong with the rib-knit and soft lining of the Salty Lined Beanie. On the slopes or on your morning commute, either will add a polished finishing touch.

    The importance of a functional winter hat cannot be overstated—think of it as the final brushstroke in the art of winter layering.
